To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pharmacokinetic of colistin is different in cystic fibrous patients compared to healthy controls.
Colistin methanesulfonate, administered as aerosol or intravenously, is rapidly absorbed, but the systemic exposure to colistiin is lower than previously reported in healthy subjects.

1) the systemic exposure to colisin after CMS administration is lower in CF patients than in healthy volunteers, 2) the systemic exposure after repeated nebulisations was very low, and 3) the PK of colistimethate and colistin after CMS administration in CF patients are comparable to that previously reported for healthy volunteers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the PK of CMS and its active metabolite colistin in plasma, urine, sputum and bronchial secretions in CF patients treated by either intravenous or nebulized administration of CMS.
the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of antibiotics used to treat cystic fibrosis.
the pharmacokinetics of colimycin in cystic fibroses patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PK of colistins in plasma is not significantly different between healthy volunteers and CF patients.
colistin PK is different in CF patients compared healthy volunteers, but that this difference is not clinically relevant.
the pharmacokinetic of colistin is not significantly different between CF patients and healthy volunteers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PK of colistimethate and colistin in cystic fibroses is comparable to healthy volunteers.
the pharmacokinetics of colimycin in CF patients is similar to those previously reported in non-CF patients.
CMS is rapidly absorbed and eliminated from the body after administration by either intravenous or nebulization route.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in CF patients, colistin is poorly absorbed after nebulization and that the use of CMS as an aerosol is not recommended.

the systemic exposure to colisti is lower in CF patients treated intravenously compared to healthy volunteers, and that the exposure to colistimethanesulphonate in the lung is much higher compared to the exposure in plasma.
, despite a lower renal clearance of colistine methanesulphate, the colistin exposure in plasma after intravenous administration of the prodrug was similar between healthy and CF patients.
